ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure is a line-angle organic structure, with several curved arrows and a separate “B:” label; according to the problem, the curved arrows are ignored. The main body is a fused bicyclic skeleton: on the left is a six-membered ring containing a ring ketone carbonyl, and on the right is a five-membered ring containing a carbonyl. The upper bridgehead carbon is connected to a methyl substituent shown with a solid wedge; the lower bridgehead carbon is connected to an OH shown with a solid wedge. There is also an independent boron atom species. Reasoning: Starting from the upper chiral bridgehead carbon bearing methyl, write as C[C@]12. Along the left six-membered ring, pass sequentially through three carbons and include the ring ketone to obtain C[C@]12CCC(=O)C, then return to the lower chiral bridgehead carbon bearing OH and close ring number 1, written as [C@@]1(O). Then from this lower bridgehead carbon, along the right five-membered ring, pass through two methylenes to the second carbonyl and close back to the upper bridgehead ring number 2, obtaining CCC2=O. Finally append the independent boron atom as a separated component as .[B].

raw_record.question_text: What is the SMILES expression of the transition-state structure shown in the image, ignoring the arrows?

method.method_draft: First describe the image as a line-angle organic structure and ignore all curved arrows as instructed. Trace the carbon skeleton starting at the bridgehead methyl-bearing carbon: write a methyl attached to a chiral bridgehead, assign two ring closure labels to that bridgehead, then follow the six-membered ring through three carbons including the ring ketone and close it at the lower chiral bridgehead bearing OH. Continue from that lower bridgehead around the five-membered ring through two methylenes to the second ketone and close back to the upper bridgehead. Encode the wedge-defined stereochemistry at the two bridgeheads as C[C@]12... and [C@@]1(O)..., and append the separate boron atom as .[B], yielding C[C@]12CCC(=O)C[C@@]1(O)CCC2=O.[B].
method.CoT_raw: 图像描述：图中是一个线角式有机结构，带有若干弯箭头和一个单独的“B:”标记；按题意弯箭头忽略。主体为稠合双环骨架：左侧是含一个环酮羰基的六元环，右侧是含一个羰基的五元环。上方桥头碳连有一个以实楔表示的甲基取代基；下方桥头碳连有以实楔表示的 OH。另有一个独立的硼原子物种。推理：从上方带甲基的手性桥头碳开始写作 C[C@]12。沿左侧六元环依次经过三个碳并包含环酮，得到 C[C@]12CCC(=O)C，然后回到下方带 OH 的手性桥头碳并闭合 1 号环，写作 [C@@]1(O)。再从该下方桥头碳沿右侧五元环经过两个亚甲基到第二个羰基并闭合回上方桥头的 2 号环，得到 CCC2=O。最后把独立硼原子作为分离组分追加为 .[B]。

planner_metadata.image_role: Read the molecular drawing: a fused bicyclic 6/5 ring system, with a ketone in the six-membered ring, a ketone in the five-membered ring, a methyl substituent on the upper bridgehead shown by a solid wedge, an OH substituent on the lower bridgehead shown by a solid wedge, and a separate boron species labeled B: with arrows to H/O. Curved arrows are present but are not part of the molecular graph.
planner_metadata.text_role: Use the question text to know the required output is a SMILES expression for the shown transition-state structure and specifically that arrows should be ignored.
planner_metadata.knowledge_role: Use line-angle conventions to infer carbons and hydrogens, represent carbonyls as C(=O), encode the two fused-ring closures with ring numbers 1 and 2, preserve the bridgehead stereochemistry using @/@@, and represent disconnected boron as a separate fragment with dot notation. Apply the instruction to omit reaction arrows/transition arrows from the SMILES graph.
